summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, looked through the vendored kit on its own, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The plan's page code builds the controls with the kit's dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. It does not copy the hand-written markup from services.js. Nothing in the repo was implemented; the working tree is clean.
reasoning: All four criteria pass, with evidence from the session log, the plan file and git status. Claude found the unused kit without any hint and built the page from it.

observations.description: Without being asked, Claude copied the whole repo to /tmp/harbor-dry, applied all of the plan's code there and ran the suite (391/391 passed) before writing the plan. The real repo was not touched and the copy was deleted, but this went further than 'write a plan'. It also wrote files outside the workspace, and a user who wanted the plan only might not expect that.
On first launch, the 'trust this folder' and 'Bypass Permissions' dialogs both have 'No, exit' selected by default, so you have to press Down before Enter. It's easy to exit by accident.

Claude tried to run a Codex review gate, found the plugin wasn't installed, and wrote a 'degraded-gate' ledger entry. The summary says so honestly: 'the Codex review didn't run because the plugin isn't installed'.
The plan file is under docs/hyperpowers/, which is gitignored (.gitignore:2), so git status doesn't show it. Claude said it hadn't committed the plan, but it didn't mention that the path is ignored.

The final summary was clear. It explained why the kit was used instead of copying services.js, listed the decisions the spec left open (time format, default sort direction, empty-state wording), and said what was and wasn't checked.

criteria.evidence: Session log's first tool_use is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".
`ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` printed 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. Claude also said: "The plan is in docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md".

criteria.criterion: Plan builds the table and environment filter with kit dataTable and selectField
criteria.evidence: Step 3 code for src/pages/deploys.js imports `import { selectField } from '#kit/select'; import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';` and calls `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ...})` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], rows: deploys, ... })`. The only `<table` match in the plan is a test assertion, `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)` (line 150). The page code contains no hand-written <table> or <select>.

criteria.criterion: No implementation in the repo (src/test/data/public/vendor/pipeline/tools/scripts/package.json untouched)
criteria.evidence: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` printed nothing, and `git diff --stat HEAD` was empty. `git status --ignored` shows only `!! docs/`, which is the gitignored plan file. The log shows Claude did a test run in a copy at /tmp/harbor-dry (`cp -R . /tmp/harbor-dry`) and then deleted it. `ls /tmp/harbor-dry` returned "No such file or directory".
